newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $64.00 per cwt early Monday were scattered and passed by owners asking $65.00 to $67.00, feedlot sources said.
The bids were $1.00 below Friday's active sales.

Friday's sales surfaced late as light trading mushroomed into large numbers as several owners who had been holding out all week for $66.00 decided to sell to keep from building a large backlog of market-ready cattle, sources said.
About 40,000-plus head sold in the Texas Panhandle and about 35,000 to 40,000 or more, in Kansas, sources in those areas said.
Showlists this week were seen large, with carryover from last week's offerings expanding market-ready supplies, sources noted.
Demand for fed cattle this week could be dampened by 'captive' supplies packers have available, especially contract cattle that became available after June 1, they said.
Outlooks for increased fed cattle numbers through the summer following active placements this spring also could weigh on prices, sources said.
However, fed cattle price declines could be tempered if beef demand remains strong for outdoor grilling features, they said.
